spec: hazard/expectation_spread_variants.py header (spec committed before execution; round-17 R17-M / referee Q6; supplementary, not gated into the headline — sensitivity companion to the committed settlement-aware amendment; liveness gate #46 target)

window.note: Jun-2022..Nov-2025 inclusive; 2023 and 2024 lie wholly inside the window, so only the 2022 clip (Jun-Dec) and the December-2025 clip admit any within-year spread sensitivity

threshold_rule: mechanical-majority survives iff null_trapped_b > 0.5 × e_variant_b (identical to the committed 'null share_E > 50%' whenever e_variant_b > 0; trivially satisfied for e_variant_b <= 0, which is flagged e_benchmark_degenerate — a negative expectations shortfall is a surplus and cannot un-survive the claim)

v1_2022_linear_back_ramp.allocation: 2022 printed annual net spread Jan–Dec with w_m ∝ m (m=1..12); the Jun–Dec window takes 63/78 of the annual net (vs 7/12 uniform); all other years uniform

v2_2025_all_front.allocation: 2025 printed annual runoff allocated entirely to Jan–Nov (all in-window; maximal in-window 2025 mass — any Jan–Nov distribution gives the same window sum); all other years uniform

v3_2025_all_december.allocation: 2025 printed annual runoff allocated entirely to December 2025 (clipped out of the window; minimal — zero — in-window 2025 mass; implausible extreme, reported as a bracket); all other years uniform

v4_2022_linear_front_ramp.allocation: 2022 printed annual net spread Jan–Dec with w_m ∝ 13−m; the Jun–Dec window takes 28/78 of the annual net; all other years uniform

d1_2025_linear_back_ramp.allocation: DIAGNOSTIC, not a pre-committed variant: 2025 printed annual runoff spread Jan–Dec with w_m ∝ m; the Jan–Nov window takes 66/78; computed solely to audit the prior read-only session's direction labels

range.note: Across the four pre-committed variants the anticipated share spans 86.08%–115.26%; pooled with the committed endpoints (uniform 88.51%, settlement-aware 75.58%) the disclosed span is 75.58%–115.26%. Every allocation leaves the anticipated share far above 50% and the null's mechanical-majority threshold intact.

direction_note: Derived direction (arithmetic, not assumption): anticipated share = (cap_target − projected_window)/cap_benchmark, so any allocation moving projected runoff INTO the Jun-2022–Nov-2025 window LOWERS the anticipated share and any allocation moving it OUT raises it. Intra-2025 the only out-of-window month is December (the Nov-2025 clip): the all-Jan–Nov front-load (V2) is the minimum over intra-2025 allocations at 86.08% and the all-December back-load (V3) the maximum at 115.26% — back-loading 2025 RAISES the anticipated share, strengthening the mechanical claim. Intra-2022 the in-window months are Jun–Dec (the back of the year): the back-ramp (V1) lowers the share to 88.05% and the front-ramp (V4) raises it to 88.98% — the same sign logic as the committed settlement-aware allocation, whose $108.2B in-window 2022 mass (vs uniform $9.3B) produces the 75.58% lower bound.

prior_reconstruction_check.label_correction: The prior read-only session reported '2022 linear back-ramp ≈ 88.05%; 2025 all-front ≈ 90.57% or 86.08% (direction labels possibly swapped)'. Derived here: 2022 linear back-ramp (V1) = 88.05%; 2025 all-front (V2) = 86.08% — the 86.08 figure is the all-front value and the 'all-front ≈ 90.57' label was WRONG; 90.57 belongs to the 2025 linear back-ramp (D1) = 90.57%. The prior 86.1–90.6 pair therefore spans all-front to linear-back-ramp intra-2025 allocations; the implausible all-December extreme (V3) = 115.26% lies outside it.
